data.name: Khairat
data.gender_notes: Khairat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Khairat is an Arabic name that means doing good deeds and charitable acts. It is a virtuous name that reflects a person's kindness and generosity. The name Khairat carries the meaning “Good deeds” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khairat usually hope their child will grow to embody good deeds and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Khairat is associated with the concept of Sadaqah, or voluntary charity, which is considered a means of purifying one's soul.
data.etymology: Khairat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Good deeds.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khairat total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khairat is often given to children in Muslim communities as a reminder of the importance of doing good deeds and helping others. It is a name that encourages kindness, generosity, and compassion, and is a source of inspiration for people to live morally and ethically. The name is also associated with the Islamic concept of cosmic justice, where good deeds are rewarded in this life and in the next.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Khairat has deep spiritual significance in Islam. It reflects the belief that every good deed, no matter how small, is a step towards Allah and a way to draw closer to Him. The name reminds us of the importance of living a virtuous life and striving to be a good person. It also reminds us of the prophetic hadith that says, "The best charity is giving in the way of Allah and the next best is giving it to the living and the next to the dead" (Bukhari). By giving and doing good deeds, we not only help others but also earn the pleasure of Allah and the rewards of the Hereafter.
